I'll think through this as the farmer would.

---

My land is 8 mu, all flat, good well water. I do wheat-maize like everyone here — we've done it this way my whole life. Two people at home, my husband sometimes works in town so mostly it's me in the field with help at busy times.

**Wheat first (winter):**

Last year I planted Jimai variety — the seed shop sells it, neighbors use it too, it stands up well when wind comes. I'll use the same, about 15 kg seed per mu because I sow a bit thick, safer that way if germination isn't good.

Before planting I spread compound fertilizer — I buy the 15-15-15 kind, 2 bags per mu (that's 100 kg), plough it in with the tractor the village machine service runs. Then in spring when wheat turns green, I topdress urea, about half a bag per mu (25 kg). That's how my neighbor does it, his wheat looks good every year.

Water: I water before winter (dong shui), then green-up water in spring, then at jointing, then at filling. Four times. Well water, I pay electricity.

Spray: once for weeds early spring, once for aphids and rust around heading, once more if I see bugs. So 3 times usually.

Yield — good year 450 kg/mu, bad year 400. I count on 450.

**Maize (summer), after wheat:**

Straight after wheat harvest in June, no tillage, just direct seed with the machine — saves time and money, everyone does it now. Xianyu or Zhengdan hybrid seed, whichever the dealer has that year.

Fertilizer: I put 1.5 bags compound (75 kg) at sowing with the seeder, then when maize is knee-high I topdress urea, about 30 kg. Maize eats a lot of nitrogen, if I'm stingy the cobs are small.

Water: summer has rain usually, but if July is dry I pump once, maybe twice. Count 2 times.

Spray: one time for armyworm and corn borer, maybe a second if pests are bad. Say 2.

Yield — 550 kg/mu is normal here.

Total fertilizer spend: maybe 2000+ yuan for the year. It's a lot but I can't save on fertilizer, the harvest pays for everything.
